description: CHARACTERIZATION FIXTURE for saga #811 (issue #816): this records that `check()` is SILENT here today. It asserts an EMPTY diagnostics list, and that emptiness is the point — do not read it as a statement about the contract. Whether it stays correct is decided by the still-open #814 ruling: a fix routed through the checker must make this fixture GAIN a diagnostic, while a fix implemented in the evaluator (#815, whose declared write-set contains no checker work) leaves it as written. Either way it must be revisited, not assumed. Fault shape B — a KNOWN command used in VALUE position (issue #716, re-parented under saga #811). This is a DIFFERENT fault from shape A and the fixtures record it separately on purpose. Here `check()` is CLEAN, not merely unconsulted: `forward` resolves fine once `turtle-rendering` is active, so no checker rule fires and there is no correct answer sitting unused. Both stages are silent. Saga #811's stated mechanism ("`check()` computes the right answer and `execute()` never consults it") is therefore true of shape A only — measured here rather than assumed. Form under test: `repeat <command> [ … ]` — the loop body never runs, so `print 1` produces nothing. `turtle-rendering` is load-bearing in this fixture's declared profile set rather than decorative: without it `forward` would itself be flagged and the empty expectation would be right for the wrong reason.
